clue.text: Defective tense

definitions.meaning: a grammatical tense for an action ongoing in the past, as in 'I was walking'

explanation.definitionFit: Flawed things fall short of perfection, and in grammar this is the name of the past continuous verb form.

clue.text: Swampy planet, hot to unknown degree

parts.note: Mars is a planet
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A swampy planet that is hot to an unknown degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Boggy, waterlogged ground like a marsh.

clue.text: English deciphering runes, in effect

indicators.note: deciphering suggests the letters of runes are worked out into a new order

explanation.surface: An Englishman decoding runes, in effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deciphering' rearranges RUNES into NSURE. 'effect' is the verb, to bring about.
explanation.definitionFit: To effect something is to bring it about, to make certain it happens.

clue.text: Loud quarrel to produce litter

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
a quarrel is a crossbow bolt

explanation.surface: A noisy row leads to rubbish being strewn about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarrel' looks like an argument, but here it is a crossbow bolt.
explanation.definitionFit: A sow gives birth to a litter of piglets; this is the verb for that.

clue.text: What offers choice of channels is close — inevitable, possibly?

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters may be put together in another order

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether a close finish is inevitable.
explanation.definitionFit: A subscription service delivered by wire offering many stations to watch.

clue.text: Switch musical number

definitions.meaning: a switch is a tress of false hair
a song from the musical Hair

explanation.definitionFit: A switch is a wig or hair extension, and a song from Hair would be a number from that show.

clue.text: Shelter of Alice's intended, despatched before rail-strike

indicators.note: before says the first piece comes ahead of the rest

parts.note: despatched means sent
RY abbreviates railway
to box is to strike with the fists

explanation.surface: A guardsman's shelter, after he is sent off before a rail strike.
explanation.walkthrough: In A. A. Milne's poem about Buckingham Palace, 'Alice is marrying one of the guard', so her intended is a soldier on guard duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A small hut in which a soldier on guard duty takes cover.

clue.text: Artist escaping from city arson

indicators.note: escaping from implies the letters break loose and rearrange

explanation.surface: A painter fleeing a fire in the city.
explanation.definitionFit: One who draws with coloured wax sticks is a kind of artist.

clue.text: Poet's always following vehicle in his way through life

indicators.note: the poetic word comes after the vehicle in the answer

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A poet who always rides behind a vehicle on his journey through life.
explanation.definitionFit: A profession or life's progress is the course a person follows through their working years.

clue.text: Outlaw in favour of journalist

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
a scribe is a writer, informally a journalist

explanation.surface: A gangster backed by a friendly reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: To outlaw something is to forbid or ban it officially.

clue.text: Quite beautiful?

explanation.definitionFit: The word works as an adverb meaning fairly and as an adjective meaning attractive.

clue.text: Unorthodox monarch we find in dailies

definitions.note: plural noun: dailies are cleaning ladies who come in each day

indicators.note: unorthodox means not conventional, so the letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: An eccentric king finds himself reading the daily newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unorthodox' rearranges MONARCH and WE. 'Dailies' looks like newspapers, but in British usage a daily is a cleaning lady who comes in daily.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a daily is a domestic cleaner, a woman hired to clean a house.

clue.text: African political party any turning out?

parts.note: Lib is short for the Liberal party

indicators.note: turning out suggests the letters of the word any are turned into a new shape

explanation.surface: Asking whether anyone will turn out for an African political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning out' is the anagram signal for the three letters after the party; Lib is short for the Liberals, a British political party.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something from Libya, a country of North Africa.

clue.text: No repeats, unusually, in this unnatural language

indicators.note: unusually means in an unexpected way, so these letters appear in a new order

explanation.surface: A language in which nothing is ever said twice.
explanation.definitionFit: An invented international tongue devised by Zamenhof, artificial rather than natural.

clue.text: Cut-longer established feature of the Oval

parts.note: a gash is a cut
older means established for longer

explanation.surface: A longstanding cut on the cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground, famous for the large gas storage tanks beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The big gas storage tanks next to the Oval are a well-known landmark there.

clue.text: A piece intended, say, to be in A flat?

parts.note: a piece is a part

indicators.note: say signals that intended is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: intended means meant

explanation.surface: A musical piece, perhaps meant to be in the key of A flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives MENT, which sounds like MEANT. 'A flat' poses as a musical key.
explanation.definitionFit: A home on one floor of a building, as in a block of flats.

clue.text: The main subject of Elgar's pictures

definitions.meaning: the main is a poetic term for the open ocean
Elgar's ... Pictures is a song cycle about the ocean

explanation.definitionFit: The main is an old word for the ocean, and Elgar's song cycle Sea Pictures depicts the ocean.

clue.text: Shed tears in Caesar's obituary

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the words Caesar's obituary

explanation.surface: Weeping over Caesar's death notice.
explanation.definitionFit: To weep noisily is to cry with gasps.

clue.text: Trouble reported with drink?

indicators.note: reported means as spoken, so the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Asking whether trouble comes with drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer is a drink.

clue.text: Their mounts can be spoiled by post-impressionists!

definitions.text: Their mounts can be spoiled by post-impressionists!

parts.words: Their mounts can be spoiled by post-impressionists!
parts.note: mounts are the hinges used to fix stamps in albums, and post-impressionists are the post office franking marks that spoil a mint item, not painters

explanation.definitionFit: Philatelists collect postage items and mount them in albums; a heavy postmark can spoil a specimen.

clue.text: Social occasion for a queen, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a gathering for work and company, like a sewing or spelling get-together
a queen is one example of an insect in a hive

explanation.definitionFit: A gathering for communal work is called this, and a queen is a hive insect of this kind.

clue.text: Strongly urge one to take part in Essex horticultural membership

indicators.note: the answer takes part in, forming part of, the run of letters in Essex horticultural

explanation.surface: Pressing someone to join an Essex gardening society.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside essEX HORTicultural; Essex is an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: To press or encourage someone earnestly to do something.

clue.text: Be in awe of Longfellow's rider

definitions.meaning: Paul ___ is the horseman of Longfellow's poem about the midnight ride

explanation.definitionFit: To venerate deeply, and the surname of the patriot horseman in Longfellow's poem.

clue.text: After centre-court, more certain he will take too much of the interest

definitions.text: he will take too much of the interest

indicators.note: after says the second piece comes after the first
centre picks the middle letter of the word court

parts.note: surer means more certain

explanation.surface: After a centre-court victory, a confident player takes all the attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interest' is money charged on a loan, not attention.
explanation.definitionFit: A moneylender who charges excessive rates of interest.

clue.text: Companies' merger arranged in secure place

parts.note: Co abbreviates company
the plural gives a second company
on means arranged, as in 'the match is on'

explanation.surface: Two firms merge after the deal is arranged in safety.
explanation.definitionFit: A protective silk case, by extension any snug safe enclosure.

clue.text: I'd go back to reading for amusement

indicators.note: go back says the letters of I'd are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: I'd gives the letters ID
a reading is an interpretation or version of a text

explanation.surface: Someone longing to return to their books for pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: Entertainment or a pastime that distracts the mind from serious things.

clue.text: A sweetheart passionately aroused

parts.note: an old flame is a former sweetheart

explanation.surface: A lover stirred up by passion.
explanation.definitionFit: Glowing with strong feeling, as though burning with emotion.

clue.text: If backing carpeting, make it safe from 26!

indicators.note: backing means the word If is written in reverse

parts.note: a carpeting is a telling-off, a reprimand

explanation.surface: Fit carpet with underlay to make the house safe from fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns IF into FI. A carpeting is British slang for a rebuke; 26 refers to the light meaning ablaze.
explanation.definitionFit: Resistant to burning, so not able to catch alight.

clue.text: Driving nail obliquely — eg into bend

indicators.note: bend means to distort into another shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions for carpentry: knock the nail in at an angle, bending it.
explanation.definitionFit: In carpentry this is the technique of hammering a nail in at a slant.

clue.text: Winning final holds attention

indicators.note: holds means one word contains another inside it

parts.note: a final is an ending
to give ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: Winning the final keeps everyone's attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Charming or appealing, as in a winning smile.
